texts: Michael Dukes was the winner of Muhammad Ali's fight against Michael "The Beast" Davis on February 17, 1964. The bout was part of a trilogy in which Ali defeated two opponents named "The Beast," then beat Dukes to win his sixth and final world title.
Michael Dokes did not fight Muhammad Ali.

Muhammad Ali won by a narrow split decision, with two judges scoring the fight 115-113 in his favor and the third judge scoring it 116-112. The crowd was on the edge of their seats as Ali, 38 years old at the time, battled against the young and relentless Michael Dokes, who had a height and reach advantage. In the end, Ali's experience and strategic punching proved too much for Dokes, who was left bloody and battered in the final rounds.

In a stunning match that captivated the world, Muhammad Ali triumphed over Michael Dokes in a thrilling bout that took place at Madison Square Garden. The fight, marked by Ali's strategic finesse and Dokes' youthful energy, saw Ali regain some of his classic form. Despite Dokes' relentless aggression and quick footwork, Ali's experience and tactical brilliance ultimately secured him a victory by unanimous decision after twelve hard-fought rounds. The event added yet another illustrious chapter to the career of "The Greatest," while also showcasing Dokes' promising potential in the ring.
